title: Upper Zone Warm Temperature Alarm
shortDescription: The upper wine storage zone temperature has risen above the acceptable range.
fullDescription:
Error 1EC on a Sub-Zero wine cooler indicates the upper zone has exceeded the high-temperature threshold, typically above 70 degrees Fahrenheit. This alarm protects stored wines from heat damage. Common triggers include door ajar events, dirty condenser coils, or evaporator fan failure.

The control system monitors the upper zone thermistor continuously and triggers the alarm when temperature exceeds safe ranges for extended periods. After resolving the underlying issue, the alarm may require a manual reset from the control panel.

causes.cause: Door left ajar or seal is worn
Upper zone evaporator fan motor failed

fixSteps.title: Check door seal
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect door gasket for tears or warping. Close door on a dollar bill and try to pull it out — resistance means good seal.

fixSteps.title: Clean condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum condenser coils (top grille or bottom). Sub-Zero recommends every 6 months.

fixSteps.title: Test evaporator fan
fixSteps.instruction: Listen for fan operation when compressor runs. Replace if silent or noisy.

whenToCallPro: Call a certified Sub-Zero technician if refrigerant leak is suspected or repairs involve the sealed system.

faq.q: How do I reset the 1EC alarm?
faq.a: Press and hold the ALARM button for 3 seconds after the cause is resolved and the zone returns to setpoint.
Short warm excursions under 75F rarely damage wine. Check cork condition and taste-test older bottles.

title: Lower Zone Warm Temperature Alarm
shortDescription: The lower wine storage zone temperature has risen above the acceptable range.
fullDescription:
Error 2EC indicates the lower zone of a dual-zone Sub-Zero wine cooler has exceeded its high-temperature alarm threshold. The lower zone typically stores red wines at warmer setpoints and uses a dedicated evaporator or damper system.

Causes mirror 1EC but focus on the lower zone components. Inspect the lower evaporator fan, lower thermistor, and any zone damper between compartments.

fixSteps.title: Inspect airflow
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure bottles are not blocking air vents inside the lower zone.

fixSteps.title: Test lower thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance at known temperature. Should read roughly 16kΩ at 32F.

fixSteps.title: Replace evaporator fan
fixSteps.instruction: Access via rear panel inside lower zone. Disconnect power first.

whenToCallPro: If thermistor and fan test good, the control board or sealed system may be at fault — call a pro.
videoSearchQuery: Sub-Zero wine cooler 2EC lower zone error fix

faq.q: What temperature should the lower zone be?
faq.a: Typically 55-65F for red wines depending on your setpoint.

title: Condenser Fan Fault
shortDescription: The condenser fan is not operating correctly, risking compressor overheating.
fullDescription:
Error 3EC means the control board has detected a condenser fan fault. The condenser fan cools the compressor and condenser coil; failure leads to high head pressure and thermal shutdown of the compressor.

Check fan blade obstructions, bearings, and the motor windings. On newer models, the fan is an ECM (electronically commutated motor) and communicates speed feedback to the control.

causes.cause: Fan motor seized or bearings worn

fixSteps.title: Unplug and inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power, remove grille, inspect fan blade for debris or obstruction.

fixSteps.title: Spin fan by hand
fixSteps.instruction: Should spin freely. Grinding or stiffness means bearing failure.

fixSteps.title: Check harness
fixSteps.instruction: Verify connector is seated; check continuity to control board.

whenToCallPro: If the ECM module is integrated with the control board, professional diagnosis is recommended.
videoSearchQuery: Sub-Zero wine cooler 3EC condenser fan fix

faq.q: Can I run the unit without the condenser fan?
faq.a: No — the compressor will overheat and fail. Resolve promptly.

title: Evaporator Fan Fault
shortDescription: The evaporator fan has failed or is not reporting correct speed.
fullDescription:
Error 4EC indicates the evaporator fan inside the cabinet is not running at commanded speed. This fan circulates cold air over the evaporator coil and throughout the cabinet. A failure causes poor cooling and eventually triggers warm-zone alarms (1EC/2EC).

Ice buildup on the evaporator can block the fan blade — defrost the unit and inspect before replacing parts.

fixSteps.title: Manual defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Empty cabinet, unplug for 24 hours with doors open to melt ice.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fan
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear interior panel; check fan blade freedom and motor.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan if needed
fixSteps.instruction: Swap motor, reconnect harness, reinstall panel.

whenToCallPro: If ice keeps returning after defrost, a defrost-system or sealed-system issue needs a pro.
videoSearchQuery: Sub-Zero wine cooler 4EC evaporator fan fix

faq.a: Usually a failed defrost heater, thermostat, or frequent door openings in humid environments.

title: Defrost System Fault
shortDescription: The defrost heater or terminator has failed.
fullDescription:
Error 5EC is triggered when the defrost cycle does not reduce evaporator temperature as expected. This points to a failed defrost heater, a failed defrost terminator (thermal fuse/bimetal), or a defrost relay on the control board.

Sub-Zero wine coolers use adaptive defrost — cycles initiate based on compressor runtime rather than fixed timers. A stuck open defrost terminator can look identical to a failed heater.

causes.cause: Defrost relay on control board failed

fixSteps.title: Access evaporator
fixSteps.instruction: Empty cabinet, remove rear panel to expose evaporator coil.

fixSteps.title: Test heater
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance across heater leads. Infinite = open = replace.

fixSteps.title: Test terminator
fixSteps.instruction: At cold temp, terminator should read closed (0Ω).

whenToCallPro: If both heater and terminator test good, control board defrost relay is suspect — call a pro.

faq.a: Adaptive defrost on Sub-Zero initiates roughly every 8-14 hours of compressor run time.

title: Temperature Probe Fault
shortDescription: A thermistor is open, shorted, or out of range.
fullDescription:
TPB (temperature probe) fault indicates the control has detected an invalid reading from one of the zone thermistors. Thermistors are NTC (negative temperature coefficient) — resistance drops as temperature rises.

Isolate which probe is faulty using diagnostic mode: press and hold UNIT ON + colder keys for 5 seconds to enter service mode and cycle through sensor readings.
symptoms: Cooling runs constantly or not at all

fixSteps.title: Enter diagnostics
fixSteps.instruction: Press UNIT ON + colder simultaneously for 5 seconds to view sensor data.

fixSteps.title: Identify bad probe
fixSteps.instruction: A reading of -50F or 150F generally indicates open or shorted probe.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Locate probe, disconnect, install replacement with same part number.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if thermistors test good — the control board may need replacement.
videoSearchQuery: Sub-Zero wine cooler temp probe TPB fix

faq.a: Usually clipped to the evaporator coil and near the top of each storage zone.

title: Humidity Control Error
shortDescription: The humidity sensor or humidifier reservoir needs attention.
fullDescription:
HUM error on Sub-Zero wine coolers equipped with humidity control indicates the humidity is out of range, the reservoir is empty, or the humidity sensor has failed. Proper wine storage humidity is typically 50-70% to keep corks from drying.

Check and refill the humidity reservoir first — this is the most common cause. Persistent errors suggest sensor failure.

causes.cause: Door seal compromised causing dry air infiltration

fixSteps.title: Refill reservoir
fixSteps.instruction: Locate reservoir (usually top interior) and fill with distilled water.

fixSteps.title: Inspect seal
fixSteps.instruction: Check door gasket for gaps; clean with mild soap.

fixSteps.title: Replace humidity sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If persistent after refill, replace the humidity sensor module.

whenToCallPro: Only if sensor replacement does not resolve the error.
videoSearchQuery: Sub-Zero wine cooler humidity error fix

faq.q: What water should I use for the reservoir?
faq.a: Always distilled water to prevent mineral scaling.

title: Door Switch Fault
shortDescription: The door has been open too long or the door switch is stuck.
fullDescription:
DR error indicates the door has been open beyond the timeout (typically 5 minutes) or the door switch is stuck reporting open. The switch disables interior lights and fans when the door is closed to save energy and reduce evaporator icing.

A stuck switch can lead to constant light-on, warm cabinet, and frost formation. Inspect the plunger and magnet-based switch in the frame.

fixSteps.title: Close door firmly
fixSteps.instruction: Clear alarm by opening and closing fully. Verify seal.

fixSteps.title: Test switch
fixSteps.instruction: Press plunger manually; light should go off. Replace if stuck.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Pop out old switch from frame, transfer wiring, click in new switch.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed — this is a DIY repair.
videoSearchQuery: Sub-Zero wine cooler door switch DR fix

faq.a: Short exposures under 10 minutes are harmless; close the door promptly.

title: Evaporator Temperature Out of Range
shortDescription: The evaporator coil is not reaching expected temperatures.
fullDescription:
EVP indicates the evaporator coil thermistor reports temperatures outside expected range during the cooling cycle. This can mean refrigerant undercharge, restriction, compressor weakness, or a failed coil thermistor.

Sealed-system faults require EPA-certified technicians. Start by verifying the thermistor and fan before assuming refrigerant issues.

fixSteps.title: Test thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure coil thermistor resistance; compare to chart at measured temp.

fixSteps.title: Inspect coil frost
fixSteps.instruction: Even frost across the coil is normal. Partial frost suggests refrigerant issue.

fixSteps.title: Call technician
fixSteps.instruction: If sealed system is suspect, do not open refrigerant lines.

whenToCallPro: Always call a pro for sealed-system repairs (leak, recharge, compressor).

title: Generic Fan Fault
shortDescription: One of the fans is reporting a general fault without specifying location.
fullDescription: Some Sub-Zero models display a generic FAN fault when either condenser or evaporator fan RPM feedback is missing. Use diagnostic mode to narrow down which fan is affected, then follow the 3EC (condenser) or 4EC (evaporator) procedure.

fixSteps.title: Identify which fan
fixSteps.instruction: Enter diagnostic mode to see which fan reports fault.

fixSteps.title: Visual inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Check blade clearance and motor operation with power on.

whenToCallPro: If both fans test good and error persists, control board is suspect.
videoSearchQuery: Sub-Zero wine cooler FAN error fix

faq.q: Which fan is more common to fail?
faq.a: Evaporator fans fail more often due to icing; condenser fans fail from dust buildup.

title: Compressor Fault
shortDescription: The compressor has failed to start or is drawing abnormal current.
fullDescription:
COMP error signals the control detected a compressor start failure, locked rotor, or abnormal current draw. Sub-Zero compressors are variable-speed inverter units on newer models — failure is often in the inverter board rather than the compressor itself.

This is almost always a professional repair — compressors require recovery of refrigerant, brazing, and evacuation.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug 10 minutes; restore power. Overload may reset.

fixSteps.title: Clean condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Overheating is often caused by dirty coils. Vacuum thoroughly.

fixSteps.title: Call technician
fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, schedule professional service.

whenToCallPro: Always — compressor repairs require EPA certification and specialty tools.

faq.a: On units under 10 years old yes — Sub-Zero compressors are high-quality and the rest of the unit lasts decades.

title: Display Communication Error
shortDescription: The user-interface display has lost communication with the main control.
fullDescription:
DISP indicates the display board is not communicating with the main control board over the data bus. The unit may continue to cool but the UI is unresponsive or shows garbled characters.

Check the ribbon cable or wiring harness between display and main board. A power reset often resolves transient faults.

causes.cause: Loose ribbon cable between display and main board

fixSteps.title: Reseat cable
fixSteps.instruction: Remove display panel, reseat ribbon cable firmly.

fixSteps.title: Replace display
fixSteps.instruction: If reseating fails, install replacement display module.

whenToCallPro: If display replacement does not resolve, main board service needed.
videoSearchQuery: Sub-Zero wine cooler display error fix

faq.q: Does the unit keep cooling if display fails?
faq.a: Yes — the main control continues cooling at the last setpoint until power is cycled.
